In Luke 10:6, Jesus instructs the seventy-two that if a household is unworthy, their peace 'will return' to them—a striking image of blessing boomeranging back. Paul promises the Ephesian elders he will return (Acts 18:21), and the heroes of faith in Hebrews 11:15 are praised for not longing to return to the country they had left."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: ""
    Enriched: To turn back or return to a place previously departed from, literally bending one's course in reverse. Spanish 'volver/regresar' and French 'retourner' capture the straightforward spatial meaning. Matt 2:12 has the Magi returning by another road; Luke 10:6 metaphorically pictures peace returning to the sender; Acts 18:21 records Paul's promise to come back; Hebrews 11:15 notes the patriarchs' refu...
    Existing Spanish translations: de-regresar, volver, volverá, volveré

}
